senses.gloss: m. (Arab. ḡuwâliḳ, Pers. ḡawâlakh = hippopera, Freytag s. v.) long pouch as a receptacle for grain, thrown over the shoulders or across an animal’s back, haversack.
units: <cite ref="Taanit 23b:10">Taan. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>הבו לי גוּאַלְקִי וכ׳</he> (Ar. … <he>קא</he>; Ms. M. 2 <he>שקיל גולקא</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 200) get me my haversack, and I shall go and buy &c.—Pl. <cite ref="C00267"><he>גּוֹאַלְקָאן</he></cite>, <he>גּוֹאַלְקֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Lamentations 5:5">Targ. Lam. V, 5</cite>.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 154b:10">Sabb. 154ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="H00110"><he>חֶבֶר</he></cite> (where Var. lect. are quoted).
<cite ref="Sukkah 20b:5">Succ. 20ᵇ</cite> <he>חזו לגואלקי</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>לגולקי</he>) are fit for haversacks.
